newsitem.title: SWEDEN: New Swedish paper complains over distribution co.
newsitem.headline: New Swedish paper complains over distribution co.

text.p: Swedish newspaper Metro Weekend said on Thursday it had filed a complaint to competition authorities over allegedly unfair practices by a distribution company owned by rival broadsheets.
Metro was set up 18 months as a free daily newspaper distributed at the city's underground stations from Monday to Friday.
But publisher MTG Publishing AB, a unit of Swedish timber- to-media conglomerate Kinnevik AB, has recently started a weekend edition and a door-to-door delivery service for subscribers.

Robert Braunerhielm, MTG's managing director, said Sweden's two main newspapers, which own the city's sole key distribution company Pressens Morgontjanst, were trying to prevent competition on the market.
Pressens Morgontjanst is owned 80 percent by Swedish daily Dagens Nyheter and 20 percent by rival broadsheet Svenska Dagbladet, Metro Weekend said in a statement.

"We would like the Swedish Competition Authority to examine whether Pressens Morgontjanst can stop new actors from entering the market because of pressure from Dagens Nyheter and Svenska Dagbladet," Braunerhielm said in the statement.
It said delivery company Pressens Morgontjanst had threathened to break a distribution contract based on the fact that it was about to lose state support from the Ministry of Culture.
